subject: Shared sizing baseline + cutover playbook for Orbit Labs Dedicated
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Torres <kevin@orbitlabs.ai>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@orbitlabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Shared sizing baseline + cutover playbook for Orbit Labs Dedicated

Kevin / Priya —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass sizing workbook and a short runbook that lays out the cutover milestones we typically run for hosted -> dedicated migrations. The two artifacts are: orbit-sizing-v1.xlsx (baseline traffic / L7 distribution / target tail-latency SLO) and cutover-runbook-v1.pdf (roles, windows, rollback gates). Also included a small set of KV-cache warm-up snippets we recommend for LLama-like workloads.

High level proposed plan (week-of):
- Week 0 (validation): Redwood runs a 48h throughput validation on dedicated staging with your representative production traces. We validate latency P50/P95/P99 and memory/KV stability.
- Week 1 (canary): 5% traffic for 24h, monitor token-cost delta and error rate; automated fallback to hosted if latency regresses >15% or error rate >0.5%.
- Week 2 (ramp): 5 -> 40% -> 100% over two business days with warmup and cache prefill windows.

Key asks from Orbit Labs for the validation run:
1) Representative trace (500k requests sampled across peak and off-peak) — spreadsheet column mapping provided in the sizing workbook.
2) Confirm target tail latency SLO (we used 450ms P95 in the workbook; update if different).
3) Any planned model variant changes (quantized vs fp16) during the window.

We intentionally sized with a 25% headroom buffer for peak shifting during the first 30 days. The workbook maps expected concurrency to GPU class (A100-40GB vs H100-80GB) and includes continuous-batching knobs we recommend.

Questions for your team:
- Is the suggested 48h staging validation acceptable?
- Can we reserve the suggested cutover weekend (Fri evening -> Sat morning) or do you prefer a weekday window?

Next steps: if you approve the baseline and the weekend window, Karthik and Neha will schedule the validation job and share the test credentials.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan@redwood.com] | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: orbit-sizing-v1.xlsx (excel), cutover-runbook-v1.pdf (pdf), kv-cache-warmup-snippets.txt (txt)

From: Kevin Torres <kevin@orbitlabs.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya.raman@orbitlabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Shared sizing baseline + cutover playbook for Orbit Labs Dedicated

Jordan —

Thanks for the thorough pack. Quick answers inline:
- 48h staging validation: yes, good by us. We can provide a sampled trace and a 24h production slice.
- SLO: we need P95 <= 400ms if possible; P99 target is 900ms (historical spikes).
- Model variant: we plan to switch to the 4-bit quantized family in the next sprint (targeting the migration), but for cutover we want parity with hosted (fp16) on day-0; we can flip to quantized once stable.

One operational ask: can Redwood pre-provision dedicated KV cache (prefill) so that first-request misses are minimized? Our customers see heavy conversational prefix reuse.

We prefer a weekend window but would like the run to end by Saturday 18:00 PT.

Kevin
Kevin Torres | Head of AI Infra, Orbit Labs
kevin@orbitlabs.ai | +1 206-555-0133

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0000
Subject: Orbit Labs: confirm staging duration, SLO delta, and prefill ask (internal)

Team —

Orbit agreed to 48h validation and asked for P95 <= 400ms (they'll accept P99 <= 900ms). They also want hosted parity on day-0 (fp16) and a subsequent flip to quantized once stable. Crucially they asked if we can pre-provision/prefill KV cache to avoid first-request cold misses.

Notes / proposed responses from infra side:
- Staging run: use sample trace + 24h slice from production; run with fp16 model binary to establish parity.
- Prefill: Neha, can we run a KV prefill job prior to the canary? If so, what duration and what ops (simple prefix replay vs synthetic warmers)?
- Capacity mapping: I'll attach the workbook to the portal job. We used A100-40GB for concurrency segments under 3.5k concurrent generation tokens/sec, and H100-80GB above that. We recommended burst policy for short spikes.

Action items:
- Neha: confirm prefill procedure and estimated time to prefill (ETA by EOD).
- Karthik: coordinate scheduling and HubSpot deal update (set cutover window Sat, Jun 26 02:00-10:00 PT tentatively).
- Marissa: post-cutover success criteria and customer comms template (include rollback messaging).

Thanks —
Jordan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:44:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Orbit Labs: confirm staging duration, SLO delta, and prefill ask (internal)

Jordan / team —

Short answers: yes, we can do an automated KV prefill. Details below and a suggested fail-safe.

Prefill plan (automation):
- Mechanism: stream selected prefixes from the sampled trace into the dedicated KV store for 30 minutes prior to canary cutover. Use parallel prefill workers to warm top-5k keys first (we'll take hot-key histogram from the trace).
- Warmup duration: 30 min for top tier; up to 2h to reach 95% key coverage depending on working set size. We'll plan for a 90-minute warm-up window before turning traffic on.
- Validation: run a synthetic burst of 500 requests hitting warmed prefixes and assert miss-rate <1.5% and mean latency delta <8% vs baseline.
- Rollback gate: if P95 latency increases >15% above staging baseline or cache miss-rate >3% for 15 consecutive minutes, auto-failover to hosted for 30m while we triage.

Sizing confirmations:
- The workbook's A100 vs H100 thresholds look reasonable but add a conservative 10% GPU cushion for the first 72hrs.
- For fp16 parity, we should reserve one extra worker node per pod to absorb any extra KV memory overhead when we flip to quantized later.

I'll prepare the prefill script and a dry-run runbook (will attach short snippets: kv-cache-warmup-snippets.txt). ETA: dry-run by Thu EOD; prefill automation ready Mon.

-Neha

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Torres <kevin@orbitlabs.ai>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@orbitlabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Shared sizing baseline + cutover playbook for Orbit Labs Dedicated

Kevin / Priya —

Thanks — quick update and requested confirmations:

1) Staging validation is scheduled for Thu 24 Jun (48h job) using your 24h production slice + sampled trace. Neha will run a dry-run of the prefill script on Thu morning.
2) Cutover window proposed: Sat 26 Jun 02:00-10:00 PT (ends by 18:00 PT as you requested; we'll leave padding). Please confirm if this is still OK.
3) SLOs: we'll aim for P95 <= 400ms; P99 <= 900ms is the acceptance target for the first 72h post-cutover. If we fail the P95 target by >15% vs staging baseline, we trigger the rollback gate.
4) Prefill: Neha confirmed automated prefill. Expect a 90-minute warm-up prior to canary traffic.

Mutual action items (short checklist):
- Orbit: provide sampled trace csv and a 24h production slice by Wed 23 Jun 10:00 PT.
- Orbit: confirm final list of model binaries for day-0 (you indicated fp16).
- Redwood: run 48h staging validation and share report (by Fri EOD).
- Redwood: execute prefill and schedule canary (Sat 02:00 PT).

If you approve, we'll lock the weekend window and begin the staging job tomorrow.

Best —
Jordan
